I am comparing two runs of the same model on the same eight NPU node. Run A used VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 and run B used VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1. Every other serve flag was identical, and both runs answered the same twelve prompts with logprobs=5. I now have, per prompt, the generated token strings and their logprobs. Please do three things. First, list the failure modes that token-identical but logprob-different outputs point to, and rank them by likelihood. Second, explain how a non-greedy sampling run with a fixed seed can still differ between two kernels. Third, propose a short numeric acceptance rule combining exact-match rate, mean per-token match rate, and maximum logprob delta, and state which of those three should gate a release.

Implement a pure function `compare_runs(a, b, max_delta)` in Python 3.10+ that takes two lists of records.
Each record is a dict with keys: id (str), tokens (list[str]), logprobs (list[float|None]), temperature (float), parsed_ok (bool).
Both lists contain the same ids in the same order; assume validation already happened. The function must return a dict with: exact_matches (int), records_compared (int), max_logprob_delta (float|None) over positions where both sides have a number, and failures (list[str]).
A record fails when tokens differ while temperature == 0, when token lists have different lengths, or when any aligned logprob delta exceeds max_delta. Non-greedy records with different tokens must not fail but must be counted separately.
Only the standard library may be used. Include type hints and a docstring; do not print.

Finish with the single experiment that would settle the argument.
